title: You Do All These Things
summary: We act like rainmakers, but we don't really know how any of it happens. The Lord makes things grow, so keep us humble and our hope in Jesus.
exhortation: In business we have a term: the rainmaker. That's the person who seems to make things happen out of nothing. Bring them in, they sprinkle fairy dust, and it all springs into action. As I reflected on this verse, I realized a lot of life feels like that. It feels like we make it happen.

We sow a crop and food springs out of the ground, and we say, "Look what we did. What a great farmer I am." The businessman looks at his success and thinks, "Look at the money I've made. I should write a book about my process, my grit, my method," just like a thousand people before him. Every year there's an endless stream of books on how to find the secret. Everyone is scrambling to build what they want for themselves.

The reality, for the farmer and the businessman, is that we don't really know how any of it happens. I know lots of people who work very hard in business. Some succeed and some don't. You put a seed in the ground and water it, and like magic, food comes out. What is that? It should fill us with amazement and gratitude. But often it just feeds my pride and my sense of self-importance, because we don't want to face the truth: the Lord makes things grow. God creates the abundance. Everything comes from his hand. Apart from him, you and I do nothing.

This is especially dangerous in our wealth- and health-saturated culture. If we're not careful, we can live in an illusion and functionally deny our own Creator. "Are there any among the false gods of the nations that can bring rain? Or can the heavens give showers? Are you not he, O Lord our God? We set our hope on you, for you do all these things."
prayer: Lord, you bring the harvest. We want to labor with all our strength: to provide for our families, train our children, grow in grace, serve others, disciple other believers, help the needy and comfort the hurting. But all good things and all fruit come from you. You are the Lord of the harvest. Keep us humble, and keep our hope in Jesus alone, not in our own strength.

May it be you alone who thrills our souls, whom our eyes look to and our hearts long for. Let us not depend on our own strength, ideas or plans. Let us hunger and thirst for your word and hide it deep in our hearts, so that we walk in your ways and not our own. As we go through our day, bring your word to mind so we can walk in it. We pray in Jesus' name. Amen.
